news.n_jpn_saigyo: They say the old poet-monk Saigyō, nearly seventy, has set off on foot for distant Hiraizumi in the north to collect gold for rebuilding Tōdaiji.
news.n_jpn_yoshitsune_flees: People whisper that the disgraced Minamoto no Yoshitsune, hero of the war against the Taira, has fled his brother's wrath to the lord of Hiraizumi in the north.
news.n_jpn_hiraizumi: News has come: Yoshitsune is dead in the north, and Yoritomo's army has destroyed the Fujiwara of Hiraizumi. The whole east now answers to Kamakura.
news.n_jpn_eisai: The monk Eisai has returned from Song China. He preaches Zen and has brought tea seeds with him.
news.n_jpn_goshirakawa: The retired emperor Go-Shirakawa has died – the man who played the Taira and Minamoto off against each other for thirty years.
news.n_jpn_todaiji: In Nara the rebuilt Great Buddha Hall of Tōdaiji has been consecrated. Shogun Yoritomo himself came with thousands of warriors.
news.n_jpn_honen: The monk Hōnen has written a book saying that calling on the name of Amida Buddha is enough for salvation. The learned monks are furious.
news.n_jpn_yoritomo_dies: Shogun Minamoto no Yoritomo has died – after a fall from his horse, they say. His young son Yoriie will become shogun.
news.n_jpn_sanetomo: A coup in Kamakura: Shogun Yoriie has been removed, his younger brother Sanetomo made shogun, and their maternal grandfather Hōjō Tokimasa runs everything.
news.n_jpn_yoriie_killed: News has come: the former shogun Yoriie has been murdered in exile at Shuzenji temple.
news.n_jpn_shinkokin: The court has compiled a new imperial poetry anthology, the Shin Kokinshū. The nobility are copying it eagerly.
news.n_jpn_genghis: Chinese merchants say that far beyond the Great Wall a certain Temüjin has united the steppe tribes and taken the name Genghis Khan.
news.n_jpn_honen_exile: Hōnen's teaching has been banned. He himself has been exiled to Shikoku, and his disciple Shinran to distant Echigo.
news.n_jpn_hojoki: The hermit Kamo no Chōmei, living in a hut in the hills, has written his Hōjōki – about fires, famine and the impermanence of all things.
news.n_jpn_wada: There were two days of fighting in Kamakura: the old warrior Wada Yoshimori rebelled against the Hōjō and perished with his whole house.
news.n_jpn_zhongdu: They say the Mongols have taken the northern capital of the Jurchen. The Chinese ports are full of refugees from the north.
news.n_jpn_sanetomo_killed: Terrible news from Kamakura: Shogun Sanetomo has been cut down by his own nephew on the steps of the Hachiman shrine. The Minamoto line is extinct.
news.n_jpn_jokyu: News from the east: in a month Kamakura's army crushed the supporters of the retired emperor Go-Toba. Go-Toba himself has been exiled to the Oki islands.
news.n_jpn_dogen_china: The young monk Dōgen has sailed for China in search of a true Zen teacher.
news.n_jpn_masako: Hōjō Masako, Yoritomo's widow, whom people called "the nun shogun" behind her back, has died.
news.n_jpn_genghis_dies: Korean sailors say the great khan of the Mongols, Genghis, has died on campaign. But his sons are not stopping.
news.n_jpn_goseibai_news: They say Kamakura has drawn up a code of laws for warriors – from now on land disputes will be judged by what is written.
news.n_jpn_jin_falls: Chinese merchants have brought news: the Mongols, together with the Song, have destroyed the Jurchen kingdom.
news.n_jpn_kamakura_buddha_start: In Kamakura they have begun building a huge statue of the Buddha – collectors are going round all the eastern provinces.
news.n_jpn_mongols_west: They say the Mongols have gone far to the west and are burning cities nobody here has ever heard of.
news.n_jpn_yasutoki_dies: The regent Hōjō Yasutoki, who drew up the warriors' laws, has died. They say he ruled justly.
news.n_jpn_eiheiji: The monk Dōgen has left the capital for the mountains of Echizen and founded a monastery there, to sit in Zen far from the world.
news.n_jpn_hoji: In Kamakura the Hōjō have destroyed the mighty Miura clan. No one rivals them now.
news.n_jpn_bronze_buddha: In Kamakura they have begun casting the Great Buddha in bronze. The copper, people say, comes from melted-down Chinese coins.
news.n_jpn_kenchoji: In Kamakura the Zen monastery of Kenchōji has opened under the Chinese monk Lanxi. And in Awa a young monk named Nichiren has begun preaching the Lotus Sutra.
news.n_jpn_baghdad: Merchants from China say the Mongols have taken and sacked the great city of the caliphs far to the west.
news.n_jpn_goryeo: After thirty years of war Korea has submitted to the Mongols. Sailors say its coasts are laid waste.
news.n_jpn_kublai: Kublai has become the new great khan of the Mongols. They say he rules from China and looks to the east.
news.n_jpn_shinran_dies: The old monk Shinran, who taught that Amida saves even the wicked, has died in Kyoto.
news.n_jpn_mongol_letter: A letter from the Mongol khan has reached Dazaifu via Korea demanding that "the king of Japan" send tribute. The regent Tokimune did not reply.
news.n_jpn_nichiren_sado: The monk Nichiren, who foretold a foreign invasion, was nearly executed and then exiled to the island of Sado.
news.n_jpn_bunei_news: News from Kyushu: the Mongols landed at Hakata and burned the town, but by morning their fleet had gone.
news.n_jpn_envoys_executed: The regent Tokimune has had the Mongol envoys executed at Tatsunokuchi. War is now unavoidable.
news.n_jpn_hangzhou: Chinese refugees say the Mongols have taken Hangzhou, the Song capital. Many learned monks are fleeing to Japan.
news.n_jpn_song_falls: The last Song emperor has perished at sea off Yamen. All of China is now under the Mongols.
news.n_jpn_koan_news: Messengers from Kyushu bring joy: a typhoon has scattered the huge Mongol fleet off Hakata. The temples hold services of thanksgiving.
news.n_jpn_engakuji: In Kamakura the monastery of Engakuji has been founded to pray for those who fell in the Mongol war, on both sides. That same year Nichiren died.
news.n_jpn_tokimune_dies: The regent Hōjō Tokimune, who repelled the Mongols, has died. He was only thirty-three.
news.n_jpn_shimotsuki: In Kamakura the Adachi clan has been destroyed: the all-powerful adviser Taira no Yoritsuna accused them of plotting.
news.n_jpn_ippen_dies: The wandering monk Ippen, who danced with the people chanting Amida's name and gave away everything he had, has died.
news.n_jpn_einin_news: News has come of a terrible earthquake in Kamakura: thousands dead, temples burned.
news.n_jpn_kublai_dies: Chinese merchants say Khan Kublai has died. Perhaps now the Mongols will leave us in peace.
news.n_jpn_yishan: An envoy has arrived from Yuan China – the monk Yishan. He was suspected of spying, but later became an abbot in Kamakura.
news.n_jpn_ships_seen: Rumour has it foreign ships were sighted off Satsuma. The shogunate again orders preparations for defence.
news.n_jpn_kagen: Turmoil in Kamakura: one of the Hōjō elders has been killed, and then his killers were executed too.
news.n_jpn_kasuga_scroll: They say a great illustrated set of scrolls of the deity's miracles – twenty scrolls of pictures – has been made for the Kasuga shrine in Nara.
news.n_jpn_bunpo: The shogunate has persuaded the two branches of the imperial house to take turns on the throne. Few believe it will last.
news.n_jpn_godaigo: Emperor Go-Daigo has ascended the throne. They say he wants to rule in person.
news.n_jpn_genko_shakusho: The learned monk Kokan Shiren has finished a history of Buddhism in Japan in thirty scrolls.
news.n_jpn_sinan_ship: A big merchant ship sailing from Ningbo to Hakata with porcelain and coins has gone missing off the Korean coast.
news.n_jpn_shochu: A plot against Kamakura has been uncovered in the capital. They say Emperor Go-Daigo himself was behind it, but courtiers took the blame.
news.n_jpn_kenchoji_ship: To raise money for repairs to Kenchōji, the shogunate has sent a trading ship to Yuan China.
news.n_jpn_genko: Emperor Go-Daigo has fled the capital to Mount Kasagi and called the warriors against Kamakura. His force has been defeated.
news.n_jpn_oki: Go-Daigo has been exiled to the Oki islands. But in the hills of Kawachi the warrior Kusunoki Masashige still fights for him.
news.n_jpn_kamakura_falls_news: Incredible news: Kamakura has fallen, the Hōjō regents are dead, and Emperor Go-Daigo is returning to the capital.
news.n_jpn_minatogawa: At the Minatogawa river Ashikaga Takauji defeated Kusunoki Masashige, who was killed. Emperor Go-Daigo has fled to the mountains of Yoshino.
news.n_jpn_takauji_shogun: The Northern Court has appointed Ashikaga Takauji shogun. The shogunate's seat is now in Kyoto, not Kamakura.
news.n_jpn_godaigo_dies: Emperor Go-Daigo has died in Yoshino. Takauji is building the monastery of Tenryūji in his memory.
news.n_jpn_tenryuji_ship: To pay for building Tenryūji, a trading ship has been sent to Yuan China – people call it "the Tenryūji ship".
news.n_jpn_shijonawate: The young Kusunoki Masatsura, son of the hero, has fallen at the battle of Shijōnawate fighting for the Southern Court.
news.n_jpn_kanno: Shogun Takauji has fallen out with his brother Tadayoshi, and the Ashikaga vassals have split into two camps. The war flares up again.
news.n_jpn_red_turbans: Chinese merchants say the "Red Turbans" have risen in China and Mongol rule is tottering.
news.n_jpn_tadayoshi_dies: Tadayoshi, the shogun's brother, has died in Kamakura. They say he was poisoned.
news.n_jpn_takauji_dies: Shogun Ashikaga Takauji has died. His son Yoshiakira has become shogun.
news.n_jpn_south_takes_kyoto: Southern Court forces have briefly occupied the capital again; the shogun fled but soon returned.
news.n_jpn_yoshiakira_dies: Shogun Yoshiakira has died. Ten-year-old Yoshimitsu has become shogun, with the counsellor Hosokawa Yoriyuki ruling for him.
news.n_jpn_ming: Chinese merchants have brought news: the Mongols have been driven out of China, and the new dynasty is called Ming.
news.n_jpn_ming_envoy: The Ming emperor has sent envoys to Kyushu demanding that the Japanese pirates plundering his coasts be stopped.
news.n_jpn_ryoshun: The shogun's governor Imagawa Ryōshun has taken Dazaifu from the Southern Court. There is war on Kyushu again.
news.n_jpn_zeami: They say the young shogun Yoshimitsu was enchanted by Kan'ami's sarugaku troupe and took his son Zeami into his retinue.
news.n_jpn_flower_palace: Shogun Yoshimitsu has built a new palace in the Muromachi quarter – the "Palace of Flowers".
news.n_jpn_hwangsan: Korean sailors say their general Yi Seong-gye has defeated a large band of Japanese pirates.
news.n_jpn_kanami_dies: The actor Kan'ami has died. His son Zeami now leads the troupe.
news.n_jpn_gozan: Shogun Yoshimitsu has confirmed a new ranking of the "Five Mountains" – the chief Zen monasteries of Kyoto and Kamakura.
news.n_jpn_toki: The shogun has put down the rebellion of the Toki house in Mino province.
news.n_jpn_meitoku: Lord Yamana Ujikiyo rebelled and marched on the capital but was killed in battle. The Yamana lands have been cut down.
news.n_jpn_joseon: Korean merchants say they have a new dynasty: the general Yi Seong-gye has made himself king.
news.n_jpn_reunion_news: They say the war of the two courts is over: the southern emperor has returned to the capital and handed over the regalia.
news.n_jpn_kinkaku: Shogun Yoshimitsu is building a villa in Kyoto with a pavilion covered in gold. They say no one has seen such a marvel.
news.n_jpn_oei_war: Lord Ōuchi Yoshihiro rebelled and holed up in Sakai. The shogun's troops stormed the town; Ōuchi was killed and Sakai burned.
news.n_jpn_tally_first: The first ships with Ming tallies have left for China. They say the shogun has called himself "King of Japan".
news.n_jpn_zheng_he: Merchants from China tell of hundreds of huge ships under the eunuch Zheng He sailing into the southern and western seas.
news.n_jpn_yoshimitsu_dies: The great shogun Yoshimitsu has died. His son Yoshimochi, they say, dislikes bowing to the Ming court.
news.n_jpn_ming_break: Shogun Yoshimochi has sent the Ming envoys away. Trade with China has stopped.
news.n_jpn_zenshu: Revolt in the east: Uesugi Zenshū has risen against the governor of Kamakura. The east is at war.
news.n_jpn_oei_invasion_news: They say a Korean fleet has attacked Tsushima. At first people thought the Mongols were back.
news.n_jpn_korean_envoy: A Korean envoy travelling through the country marvelled that here they take three harvests a year from a single field.
news.n_jpn_shocho_news: Peasants and carters around the capital have risen: they are smashing the moneylenders and demanding debts be cancelled.
news.n_jpn_yoshinori: The new shogun has been chosen by lot before the god Hachiman – the former monk Yoshinori. And in the south, on the Ryukyus, King Shō Hashi has united the islands.
news.n_jpn_tally_resumed: Shogun Yoshinori has resumed trade with the Ming. The merchants of Hakata and Sakai are fitting out ships again.
news.n_jpn_eikyo: The governor of Kamakura, Ashikaga Mochiuji, rebelled against the shogun, was defeated and took his own life.
news.n_jpn_kakitsu: Terrible news: Shogun Yoshinori was murdered at a banquet in the house of Lord Akamatsu. And the peasants around the capital have won an edict cancelling debts.
news.n_jpn_tsushima_treaty: The lord of Tsushima has made a treaty with Korea: a fixed number of ships a year may trade in Korean ports.
news.n_jpn_hangul: Korean merchants say their king has devised a new script so simple it can be learned in a morning.
news.n_jpn_tumu: Chinese merchants tell something unthinkable: the Oirat nomads have captured the Ming emperor himself. And here the young Yoshimasa has become shogun.
news.n_jpn_kyotoku: In the east the governor of Kamakura has killed the Uesugi deputy. They say the east will not be at peace for many years.
news.n_jpn_koshamain: News from the north: on the island of Ezo the Ainu, led by Koshamain, have risen against the Japanese settlers.
news.n_jpn_tokusei_again: Once again the peasants around the capital are rising to demand debt cancellation. The moneylenders are hiring guards.
news.n_jpn_honganji_burned: The monks of Mount Hiei have wrecked the Honganji temple at Ōtani. Its head, Rennyo, has fled.
news.n_jpn_onin_news: News has come: war has broken out in the capital – Hosokawa against Yamana. Palaces and temples are burning.
news.n_jpn_yoshizaki: The monk Rennyo has settled at Yoshizaki on the Echizen coast; thousands of Ikkō believers are flocking to him.
news.n_jpn_leaders_die: Both leaders of the war in the capital – Yamana Sōzen and Hosokawa Katsumoto – have died. Yet the war goes on.
news.n_jpn_onin_ends: The armies have left the capital for the provinces. The Ōnin War is over – but only half of Kyoto is left.
news.n_jpn_ginkaku: The former shogun Yoshimasa is building himself a villa in the Eastern Hills where he drinks tea and admires the moon.
news.n_jpn_yamashiro_ikki: In Yamashiro province local warriors and peasants have driven out the armies of both feuding lords and now govern themselves.
news.n_jpn_kaga: Unheard of: in Kaga province the Ikkō believers have overthrown Lord Togashi. They say peasants rule it now.
news.n_jpn_yoshimasa_dies: The former shogun Yoshimasa has died – the man under whom the capital burned and tea and painting flourished.
news.n_jpn_meio_coup: Hosokawa Masamoto has deposed the shogun and installed his own man. And in the east a certain Ise Shinkurō has seized Izu province.
news.n_jpn_odawara: They say the same Ise Shinkurō has taken Odawara castle by a ruse. Common folk praise him for his low taxes.
news.n_jpn_meio_quake: A great earthquake and wave have struck the Tōkai coast. They say in Kamakura the wave washed away the hall of the Great Buddha.
news.n_jpn_gion_revived: For the first time in over thirty years the Gion festival has been held in Kyoto again. The townspeople raised the money for the floats themselves.
news.n_jpn_masamoto_killed: The all-powerful Hosokawa Masamoto has been murdered by his own adopted sons. The capital is in turmoil again.
news.n_jpn_sanpo: In the Korean ports Japanese traders rose up against mistreatment. Korea has closed its ports to Japanese.
news.n_jpn_malacca: Chinese sailors say that far to the south long-nosed men from the west have taken the trading city of Malacca with cannon.
news.n_jpn_portuguese_canton: They say the same westerners – "Franks" – have sailed to Canton and are demanding trade with China.
news.n_jpn_ningbo: In the Chinese port of Ningbo the envoys of the Ōuchi and Hosokawa came to blows over the right to trade and caused a massacre. China is furious.
news.n_jpn_iwami: The Hakata merchant Kamiya Jutei has opened a rich silver mine in Iwami province.
news.n_jpn_haifuki: A new smelting method has been brought from Korea to the Iwami silver mine. Silver output has multiplied.
news.n_jpn_tenbun: News has come: the monks of Mount Hiei have burned the Nichiren temples in the capital, and half the lower city with them.
news.n_jpn_dosan: In Mino, they say, Saitō Dōsan, the son of an oil merchant, has driven out his lord and made himself the ruler.
news.n_jpn_tanegashima: Strange news from the south: a junk carrying foreigners has washed up on Tanegashima, and they have iron tubes that hurl thunder.
news.n_jpn_last_tally: The last ship sailing under Ming tallies has left for China. They say there will be no more.
news.n_jpn_xavier: A foreign monk from the west – Francis – has landed at Kagoshima and is preaching an unknown god.
news.n_jpn_ouchi_fall: In Yamaguchi the retainer Sue Harukata has overthrown Lord Ōuchi Yoshitaka. The China trade the Ōuchi ran is finished.
news.n_jpn_kawanakajima_news: The lord of Echigo, Nagao Kagetora, has marched against Takeda Shingen. They say each considers himself invincible.
news.n_jpn_itsukushima: On the island of Itsukushima Mōri Motonari has destroyed the Sue army. The Mōri are rising in the west.
news.n_jpn_macau: They say the Portuguese have settled at Macau and now carry Chinese silk to Japan in exchange for our silver.
news.n_jpn_okehazama: Unthinkable: the young Oda Nobunaga with a handful of men attacked Imagawa's huge army in a storm and killed Yoshimoto himself.
news.n_jpn_kenshin: Nagao Kagetora has taken the name Uesugi and the title of Kantō deputy. There has been another terrible battle at Kawanakajima.
news.n_jpn_omura: Lord Ōmura Sumitada on Kyushu has become a Christian – the first lord to do so.
news.n_jpn_yoshiteru_killed: Shogun Yoshiteru has been killed in his own palace by Miyoshi men. Shoguns are now playthings in others' hands.
news.n_jpn_nobunaga_news: Oda Nobunaga has entered the capital and made Ashikaga Yoshiaki shogun.
news.n_jpn_frois: They say Nobunaga has received the Portuguese padre Fróis and allowed the Christians to preach in the capital.
news.n_jpn_anegawa: At the Anegawa river Nobunaga and Tokugawa have defeated the Azai and Asakura armies.
news.n_jpn_hiei_news: Nobunaga has burned the monastery on Mount Hiei together with its monks. People are horrified.
news.n_jpn_nagasaki: Lord Ōmura has given the Portuguese the harbour of Nagasaki. Every year the "black ship" from Macau comes there.
news.n_jpn_muromachi_end: Nobunaga has driven Shogun Yoshiaki from the capital. They say the Ashikaga shogunate is finished. And in Kai, Takeda Shingen has died.
news.n_jpn_nagashino: At Nagashino Nobunaga's gunners, firing volleys from behind a palisade, mowed down the famous Takeda cavalry.
news.n_jpn_azuchi: Nobunaga is building Azuchi castle on the shore of Lake Biwa – with a seven-storey tower painted in gold.
news.n_jpn_kenshin_dies: Uesugi Kenshin, lord of Echigo, has died. His two adopted sons are already fighting over the inheritance.
news.n_jpn_ishiyama_ends: The fortress of Ishiyama Honganji has surrendered to Nobunaga after ten years of siege.
news.n_jpn_tensho_embassy: Four young Christians from Kyushu have sailed from Nagasaki for distant Rome, to the head of the Christian faith.
news.n_jpn_osaka_castle: Hashiba Hideyoshi has defeated Shibata Katsuie at Shizugatake and begun building a huge castle in Osaka.
news.n_jpn_komaki: Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu faced each other for half a year at Komaki and parted in peace.
news.n_jpn_kampaku: Hideyoshi, the son of a common ashigaru, has received from the court the title of kampaku – imperial regent.
news.n_jpn_toyotomi: The emperor has granted Hideyoshi a new surname, Toyotomi, and the highest rank of grand minister.
news.n_jpn_kitano: Hideyoshi has held a great tea gathering at Kitano: he invited everyone from lords to peasants, so long as they brought a cup.
news.n_jpn_odawara_falls: Odawara castle has fallen. Hideyoshi has united the whole country – for the first time in over a century.
news.n_jpn_rikyu: The Sakai tea master Sen no Rikyū has taken his own life on Hideyoshi's order. Nobody really knows why.
news.n_jpn_yi_sunsin: Bad news from Korea: the Korean admiral Yi Sun-sin is sinking Japanese supply ships one after another.
news.n_jpn_hideyori: A son, Hideyori, has been born to Hideyoshi. They say the old ruler is beside himself with joy.
news.n_jpn_fushimi_quake: A strong earthquake has destroyed Hideyoshi's new castle at Fushimi and the Great Buddha in the capital.
news.n_jpn_nagasaki_martyrs: In Nagasaki, on Hideyoshi's order, twenty-six Christians – friars and lay people – have been executed.
news.n_jpn_hideyoshi_dies: Toyotomi Hideyoshi has died. The armies are coming home from Korea, and the five elders are already eyeing each other.
news.n_jpn_adams: They say a ship of red-haired foreigners – not Portuguese – has wrecked off Bungo. Ieyasu keeps its pilot at his side.
news.n_jpn_edo_shogun: Tokugawa Ieyasu has become shogun. His seat is in distant Edo, in the east.
news.n_jpn_hidetada: Ieyasu has passed the title of shogun to his son Hidetada and rules from his castle at Sunpu.
news.n_jpn_ryukyu_satsuma: Shimazu troops from Satsuma have conquered the kingdom of Ryukyu.
news.n_jpn_christian_ban: The shogunate has banned Christianity throughout the country and expelled the padres. Churches are being torn down.
news.n_jpn_osaka_falls: Osaka castle has fallen. Toyotomi Hideyori is dead, and the house of Toyotomi is no more.
news.n_jpn_ieyasu_dies: Tokugawa Ieyasu has died. They say he will be enshrined as a deity.
news.n_jpn_iemitsu: Iemitsu, grandson of Ieyasu, has become shogun.
news.n_jpn_sankin: The shogun's decree: every lord must live in Edo every other year and keep his wife and heir there permanently.
news.n_jpn_shimabara: In Shimabara Christian peasants have risen under banners bearing crosses. A huge army is being sent against them.
news.n_jpn_portuguese_banned: Portuguese ships have been forbidden to come to Japan. Of the westerners, only the Dutch are allowed to trade.
news.n_jpn_dejima: The Dutch have been moved to the tiny island of Dejima in Nagasaki harbour.
news.n_jpn_ming_falls: Chinese refugees say Beijing has fallen, the last Ming emperor has hanged himself, and the Manchus rule China.
news.n_jpn_meireki: A great fire in Edo: most of the city and the castle keep have burned. They say tens of thousands died.
news.n_jpn_koxinga: The Ming general Zheng Chenggong, son of a Japanese mother, has driven the Dutch from Taiwan.
